info.title: Checkfu API
info.description: Managed agents API for managing agents, environments, sessions, automations, artifacts, and vaults.

schema.description: Idempotency-Key header. Required: resending the request with the same key returns the automation the first request created, so a lost response never leaves a second schedule running

post.description: Create an automation that runs an agent on a cron schedule. Each run starts a new session in the configured environment and sends the initial events.

description.description: What the automation is for, up to 2048 characters

agent.description: Agent to run in each session. Pass an ID to pin the latest version, or pass an object with type "agent", id, and version to pin a specific version.

environment_id.description: Environment ID each run's session uses

initial_events.description: Initial events sent when each run creates a session. Supply one text user.message event.

schedule.description: When the automation fires: a cron expression that names a single minute, so it fires at most once per clock hour, read in an IANA time zone name such as America/New_York

repeatArrayField.description: The initial user.message event sent to each session, as JSON, YAML, or @file

examples.command: checkfu automations create --name "Morning report" --agent agent_123 --environment-id env_456 --initial-event '{"type":"user.message","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Write the morning report."}]}' --schedule '{"type":"cron","expression":"0 9 * * 1-5","timezone":"America/New_York"}'
examples.description: Run an agent at 09:00 New York time on weekdays

schema.description: Opaque page token from the previous response's next_page.
Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 50)
Sort order by creation: asc (oldest first, the default) or desc
Include archived results: true or false (default false)
Only automations that use this agent

next_page.description: Token for the next page, or null when there are no more results.

get.description: List automations in creation order, oldest first by default. Archived automations are left out unless include_archived is true. The list catches up shortly after a create or archive, so an automation missing from it does not mean its create failed: to find out, resend the create with its original idempotency key, which returns the automation it created.
Retrieve an automation by ID

post.description: Change any of an automation's fields; the ones left out keep their values. Changes apply to runs that start after the update, and on an active automation a new schedule replaces the next firing. An archived automation can't be updated.

description.description: New description. To clear it, send null for description in a JSON or YAML body on stdin; the --description flag always sends text.

agent.description: Agent to run in each session. Pass an ID to pin the latest version, or pass an object with type "agent", id, and version to pin a specific version.

environment_id.description: Environment ID later runs' sessions use

initial_events.description: Initial events for future runs. Supply one text user.message event.

schedule.description: New schedule, with the same rules as on create. A field left out keeps its value, so the expression and the timezone can change separately. On an active automation the next firing moves to it.

repeatArrayField.description: The user message later runs start with, as JSON, YAML, or @file

post.description: Pause scheduled runs. You can still run the automation manually, and sessions from earlier runs continue.
Resume an automation's schedule from now, without running the occurrences it missed
Archive an automation so it never runs again
Trigger an automation run outside its schedule, including while paused. The response gives the queued run number. The run appears in history once session creation succeeds or fails.

The version served, or null when the latest version is served

post.description: Create an artifact from a set of files (version 1). A version holds at most 1000 files, 100 MiB each and 1024 MiB in total. Content sent inline in JSON is at most 1 MiB per file and 4 MiB per request, in a body of at most 16183296 bytes; upload larger files with PUT /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/blobs/{sha256} and name them by sha256.

path.description: Relative path inside the artifact, for example index.html or assets/app.js

content.description: File content: text, or base64 when encoding is base64

content_type.description: Media type; inferred from the path extension when omitted

files.description: Every file of version 1. Leave it out to create an empty artifact at version 0, upload large files with PUT /v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/blobs/{sha256}, then add version 1

repeatArrayField.description: File as JSON, YAML, or @file with path, content, and optional encoding and content_type (repeatable)

files.description: Every file of the version; a new version replaces the whole set. Send a small file's content inline, or name bytes the artifact already holds by their sha256

get.description: Download one file of an artifact version as its raw bytes, with its content type

schema.description: sha256 of the bytes, as lowercase hex

put.description: Store raw bytes in an artifact under their sha256, so a version can name them by sha256 without sending them inline. The request needs a Content-Length header, and the bytes must match the sha256 and be at most 100 MiB. Uploading bytes the artifact already holds checks them and stores nothing new.
put.summary: Upload file bytes to an artifact

The version served, or null when the latest version is served

post.description: Serve an artifact at a public address that anyone who has it can view. Publishing again changes the version served and keeps the address; after an unpublish, the next publish gets a new address. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key is not applied again, so it cannot undo a later unpublish; the same key with another version, or one used to unpublish, answers 409

delete.description: Delete a vault and its credentials. Every secret in the vault is erased before this answers; custody.erasing counts the credentials whose records have not caught up yet, and sending the delete again returns the current count. A 503 means the delete is recorded but the erasure is not confirmed: send it again.

post.description: Archive a vault and its credentials. Every secret in the vault is erased before this answers; custody.erasing counts the credentials whose records have not caught up yet. A 503 means the archive is recorded but the erasure is not confirmed: send it again.

post.description: Archive a credential. Its secret is erased before this answers. A 503 means the archive is recorded but the erasure is not confirmed: send it again.

held.description: Active credentials whose secrets are held

erasing.description: Archived or deleted credentials whose secrets are not yet confirmed erased

anyOf.description: A user message in the session conversation, with text content blocks.
An interrupt that stops the agent's current turn.
The agent is processing a turn.

name.description: The tool the model called. A code mode script is one call named codemode: its code is the input and its output the result; the calls the script makes are not published separately.

anyOf.description: The agent called a tool. A turn's calls come before its end event, whether the turn replied, failed or was interrupted.
The result of a tool call, including why the call was rejected when applicable. A turn's calls come before its end event, whether the turn replied, failed or was interrupted.

evaluated_permission.description: allow: the call ran without asking. ask: it waited for a confirmation.

anyOf.description: Records an MCP call the model made. A turn's calls come before its end event, whether the turn replied, failed or was interrupted.
Records what an MCP call the model made returned, or, with rejected, why it did not run. A turn's calls come before its end event, whether the turn replied, failed or was interrupted.
The agent's response, with text content blocks.
A model request finished. Includes token usage in model_usage.

event_ids.description: The IDs of the tool call events waiting for an answer. Send a user.tool_confirmation for each agent.mcp_tool_use and a user.custom_tool_result for each agent.custom_tool_use.

cancelled_event_ids.description: The IDs of the tool calls still waiting for an answer when the turn ended. The end of the turn cancelled them: they can no longer be answered.

anyOf.description: The agent stopped processing a turn. See stop_reason for why it stopped.
An error occurred while processing a turn. Includes the error and its retry status.

cancelled_event_ids.description: The IDs of the tool calls still waiting for an answer when the turn ended. The end of the turn cancelled them: they can no longer be answered.
